ruling.recommended_action: Refund $3.05 (voucher) for the non-exempt off-route kilometre; no account flag (no prior upheld route dispute).
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is RydeTAXI, metered, so extra distance enters the fare and any non-exempt off-route kilometre is refundable under RD-2. The trace settles that one off-route segment exists [F3] (RD-1 ✓) and that no qualifying traffic incident existed on the replaced stretch [F14] (RD-4(a) ✗; the Pan Island Expressway band 2 record [F12] is speed-band evidence only and does not exempt on its own under RD-4(b)). The only open elements are RD-5 consent scope, RD-3, and the SAFE-1 screen.

Consent: the driver asked before the segment, at 12:24, whether to take another way because of the jam ahead [F8], and the rider replied at 12:25, before the segment began at 12:27, "随便你，哪条快走哪条，我赶时间" [F9]. That is a rider message sent before the segment and is a GENERAL route authorisation — "take whichever way is faster" — which under RD-5 covers a route chosen to reach the destination [F9]. The driver's after-the-fact statement describing the same agreement [F11] adds nothing that the chat does not already show (G11). The rider now says she does not believe that way was faster, but a general authorisation is judged by scope, not by whether the driver's route in fact turned out fastest [F9][RD-5].

That authorisation, however, does not exempt the whole deviation. The optimal route runs 15.1 km against an actual 18.0 km (+2.9 km) [F1], yet the measured off-route segment accounts for only 2.16 km (4.90 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.75 km) [F3]. "Whichever way is faster" covers the route the driver chooses to reach the destination; the roughly 0.7 km of deviation not captured by the measured segment is unreconciled excess and is not refundable under RD-2, which excludes mileage swings and matching jitter not attributed to any segment. Refund is therefore limited to the segment's extra kilometres, not the whole excess-distance charge [F1][F3][RD-2].

RD-3 does not apply to excuse anything here: no stop was measured in the segment [F3], and the rider named no place; the words exchanged were a route authorisation, not a request to stop somewhere [F8][F9][RD-3(a)].

Amount: the trip's per-kilometre rate is its distance fare divided by its distance km = $25.39 ÷ 18.01 km = $1.4099…/km, stated in the fare record as $1.4098/km [F4][F7][RD-2]. The segment's extra km are 2.16 [F3]. 2.16 km × $1.4098/km = $3.0452, rounded to $3.05 [F3][F4][RD-2]. The waiting charge $0.11 [F5] is a meter waiting unit on a RydeTAXI and is not refundable under RD-3(c).

Account action: the driver has 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days [F17], so the RD-6 condition (prior upheld route dispute in 90 days) is not met and no account flag is added [F17][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages [F8][F9] and the driver's statement [F11]; they contain a complaint about fare, a route offer and a rider's assent, with no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so safety_concern is none (SAFE-1, SAFE-2).

Evidence: the chat is complete and every message is timestamped [F10], the segment is measured [F3], and the fare components are recorded [F4][F7], so the record settles every element this ruling needs [F10][F3][F4].

rejected_claims.reason: Rider asks for no_action on the basis that the way driven was not faster, but the authorisation she sent at 12:25 was 'take whichever way is faster' [F9], a general route authorisation accepted before the segment started [F8][F9]; RD-5 does not require the chosen route to prove out as fastest. No_action on the whole fare cannot stand, but the rider's underlying fare complaint succeeds in part for the one segment kilometre not covered by any authorisation reconciliation of the 2.9 km excess [F1][F3][RD-2].

The driver's blanket position that the entire deviation is excused rests on his after-the-trip statement that the rider agreed to any faster way [F11]; a driver's claim of agreement is not consent (G11), and the only rider consent on the record is the general authorisation [F9]. General authorisation covers the route chosen, so it excuses the measured segment [F3], but it does not convert the unreconciled 0.7 km of the 2.9 km excess into a waiver under RD-2 [F1][F3][F9][RD-2][RD-5].

segment_findings.reason: The driver asked before the segment whether to take another way [F8] and the rider sent a message before 12:27 authorising '哪条快走哪条' [F9]; this is a general route authorisation covering the route chosen to reach the destination, not a driver errand or a loop to nowhere, so the segment's extra kilometres are exempt under RD-5.
